text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Edge gateway 5xx spike detected across us-east-1 ingress (502/504/timeouts). error rate 18% over last 3m. Threshold crossed. Pager triggered to oncall.
Maya: picking this up, oncall here. seeing 504s and upstream timeouts from origin-pool-a.
Jamal: I'm on-call, will join in 2min. can someone drop the top-level error rate/traffic numbers? :eyes:
Maya: quick summary: 3m windows: total reqs ~125k/min, 5xxs ~22k/min, p95 latency bumped to 1.2s -> 2.8s. Affected routes: /api/v1/generate (high), /chat/stream (medium). CDN request logs show increased connection resets to edge nodes.
Priya: I can look at onboarding traffic routing, 2 min.
Lucas: adding my view — we rolled a routing tweak 12m ago to change fanout logic for context-prefetch. suspecting a fanout amplification to an internal realtime-cache cluster.
Maya: note: recent deploys: ingress-proxy 2.18.1 00:05 UTC (12m ago). Could be it.
Jamal: running quick checks. running: `kubectl get pods -n ingress -l app=edge-proxy -o wide`
Jamal: result snippet:
```
edge-proxy-1   Ready  2/2  1h  10.0.5.21  us-east-1a
edge-proxy-2   CrashLoopBackOff  0/2  11m  10.0.5.22  us-east-1b
edge-proxy-3   Ready  2/2  45m  10.0.5.23  us-east-1c
```
Maya: CrashLoopBackOff on a couple of pods. logs show repeated upstream timeouts and `recv() failed` from the kernel.
Elena: grabbing logs from edge-proxy-2: `kubectl logs edge-proxy-2 -n ingress --previous` shows spam of `upstream conn reset`.
Priya: checking internal kv-cache cluster (cache-a): metrics show spike in connection open, then drops. looks like clients are hammering multiple keys because of a cache invalidation event.
Lucas: That matches the fanout change — we started prefetching multiple keys in parallel; if cache returns errors, each upstream request times out then retries -> amplification.
Maya: impact: B2B customers with high concurrency (tenant: BrightChat) experiencing 60-80% failures; general traffic ~15-20% global failure rate.
Jamal: mitigation options (fast): 1) rollback ingress-proxy to 2.18.0, 2) temporarily disable prefetch fanout, 3) enable circuit-breaker on cache upstream in proxy, 4) shift a portion of traffic to us-west region.
Maya: I'm going to coordinate immediate action: disable prefetch flag via runtime config (no deploy) to stop parallel fanout. Patch command: `kubectl -n ingress set env deployment/edge-proxy PREFETCH_PARALLEL=false`
Jamal: executing now.
```
kubectl -n ingress set env deployment/edge-proxy PREFETCH_PARALLEL=false
kubectl rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy -n ingress
```
Elena: restart in progress, i'm tailing pods.
Priya: also scaling up ingress replicas to absorb backlog: `kubectl scale deployment/edge-proxy --replicas=6 -n ingress`
Lucas: adding quick nginx config change to lower `proxy_connect_timeout` to 1s for cache upstream and reduce `proxy_next_upstream_tries` to 1 so we avoid fanout retries. pushing via configmap patch.
Maya: please hold on further changes unless necessary; want to observe effect of prefetch toggle + scale.
Jamal: post-action check in 2m.
Maya: metrics update (1m after): error rate dropped from 18% -> 9%, p95 latency from 2.8s -> 1.4s. still elevated but improving. :thumbsup:
Elena: logs show reduced `upstream conn reset` frequency by ~70%.
Priya: customer impact partial: BrightChat still seeing 30% failures; looks like some requests are hitting unhealthy upstream nodes. continuing.
Jamal: I'll run a targeted cordon/drain on the pod that was CrashLoopBackOff (edge-proxy-2) to ensure it doesn't get traffic.
Jamal: `kubectl cordon node/us-east-1b && kubectl drain node/us-east-1b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Maya: noted; removing the bad node from rotation.
Maya: Ops note: opened internal incident ticket INC-2026 with brief cause hypothesis (prefetch + cache invalidation => upstream storm). assigning SRE and Eng-runtime.
Lucas: Eng-runtime looking at patch to add per-request fanout semaphore to avoid unlimited parallel prefetches.
Priya: reaching out to support to notify top 5 customers — sending templated update now. Template: "We're investigating elevated 5xxs affecting API traffic, mitigation underway, expected partial restoration in <30m." Will cc account success.
Elena: CDN-level mitigation idea: enable origin keepalive and reduce edge worker concurrency for this route via CDN rules to smooth bursts.
Maya: thumbs — implement after stabilization.
Jamal: current ask: Should we fail-open prefetch entirely for tenants flagged as high-fanout (feature flag)? That would reduce latency and degrade quality but lower errors.
Lucas: yes, fail-open for now for non-critical tenants. We'll add a feature-flag rollout: `FF_PREFETCH_FAILOPEN=tenant_whitelist`.
Maya: update 10m after initial: error rate now ~3.5%, BrightChat down to 8% failures. Rolling window shows traffic stabilizing.
Priya: support update sent to top customers at +12m. no escalations yet.
Jamal: handing off oncall to Priya, I'm stepping out for next meeting. Priya is taking pager.
Priya: taking oncall. I'll monitor for next 30m and coordinate with eng-runtime on the semaphore patch.
Maya: summary for this thread: root cause likely the ingress prefetch fanout change interacting with a cache invalidation wave causing upstream connection storms -> amplified retries -> edge overload -> 502/504 surge. Immediate mitigations: disabled prefetch parallelism, scale ingress replicas, cordoned bad node, adjusted nginx timeouts. Medium-term: add semaphore at runtime, circuit breakers on cache, increase observability on per-tenant fanout.
Elena: exporting logs and snapshots to the incident ticket: `s3://redwood-incidents/2975302468/logs.tar.gz`
Priya: follow-ups: (a) postmortem doc (owner: Lucas) due in 72h, (b) infra ticket to add canary + throttling for prefetch feature (owner: Eng-runtime), (c) support playbook updates for notifying customers and exposure thresholds (owner: SupportOps).
Maya: closing live triage. If infra changes needed I'll re-open. Good catch everyone. :raised_hands:
incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, status=mitigated -> monitoring. Link: https://pager.example/incident/2975302468"
